notes.decision: Translated 'that Panaretos — the last,' identifying ⲡⲓⲁⲛⲁⲣⲉⲓⲁⲥ as the All-Virtuous (cosmic eschatological figure) per accumulated glossary entry for ⲡⲓⲁⲛⲁⲣⲉⲓⲁⲥ, distinguishing it from the homophonous 'extraction/lifting-out.' The 'last Panaretos' fits the eschatological residue-context: the remainder of the cosmos is built and added upon this terminal figure.

The passage describes 'two deaths' — the first 'temporary' (ⲡⲣⲟⲥⲟⲩⲁⲓϣ = Greek πρὸς ὥραν 'for an hour'), the second 'forever' (ϣⲁⲁⲛⲏⲍⲉ). The phrase ⲉⲧⲉ ⲛ̄ⲧⲁϩ ⲡⲉ ⲡⲙⲁⲍⲥⲛⲉⲩ 'which is itself the second' echoes Revelation 20:14 'second death' — the Manichaean adoption of this eschatological commonplace.

Read ⲡⲡⲓ̈ⲱⲟⲩ as Lyc. orthographic variant of ⲡⲉⲟⲟⲩ 'the glory.' The phrase 'the glory which sheds light upon the cosmos' is in apposition to ⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓ̈ⲛⲉ 'the Light' from which the sinners' souls are stripped. The directional ⲁⲡⲕⲟⲥⲙⲟⲥ (line 9) completes ⲡⲣⲟⲩⲁⲓ̈ⲛⲉ ⲁ- 'shines upon.'

Tentatively read as ⲥⲁⲛⲟⲩϣ 'be nourished' in third negative parallel (after stripped of Light, separated from Air). The pattern of three losses — Light, Air, Soul — fits standard Manichaean eschatology of the soul cut off from the three Living Elements.

notes.decision: Read ϣⲃ̄ as the abbreviated form of ϣⲃ̄ⲓⲁⲓⲧ 'altered, different, strange' (cf. accumulated glossary). The phrase: 'these (disciples) for whom no strange-mysteries are in his knowledge' = his disciples are co-initiated, no mystery is hidden from them. Alternative reading 'fellow-mysteries' (ϣⲃⲏⲣ-) yields awkward sense with negation.

Translated literally 'that they should cease willing to be.' ⲟⲩⲟ́ⲱ = ⲟⲩⲱ 'cease, stop' + ⲟⲩⲱϣ 'desire/will' + ⲛ̄ϣⲱⲡⲉ 'to be/exist.' The construction emphasizes the immutable existence of the three works — they cannot stop willing themselves into being because they bind the Darkness within. Repeated verbatim in line 30 to close the argument.
